subject: Constitutional Law
title: 1. Definition, Scope and Basic Constitutional Concepts

segments.text: Constitutional law governs the basic institutions of the state, their powers, the limits on those powers and the rights of individuals.

Conventions are non-legal political practices that help constitutional systems operate. Rule of law means public power must be exercised according to law rather than arbitrary will. Due process broadly requires lawful and fair procedures when the state affects rights, liberty or property.

blocks.text: Constitutional law as the law of public power

segments.text: Constitutional law answers four connected questions: who may exercise public power, how that power is distributed, what procedures constrain it, and what rights limit it. A constitution therefore performs both an enabling function and a limiting function. It creates institutions and gives them authority, but it also places authority inside a legal structure.

The distinction between a constitution and constitutional law is useful. The constitutional text may be the central legal instrument, but constitutional law also includes authoritative judicial interpretation, legislation made under the constitution, conventions and institutional practices to the extent recognized by the legal system.

blocks.text: Conventions, rule of law and due process

segments.text: Constitutional conventions are practices that regulate political conduct even though their enforcement may be political rather than judicial. They are especially important in parliamentary systems because a legal power may be exercised according to an accepted constitutional practice that narrows how the power is used in ordinary circumstances.

Rule of law requires more than formal equality. It demands lawful authority, non-arbitrary government, legal accountability, access to independent adjudication and predictable application of law. Due process adds the idea that state action affecting important interests should be taken through fair, lawful procedures. Notice, an opportunity to respond, impartial decision-making and reasoned legal authority are recurring features of procedural fairness.

A formal approach asks whether government acts through validly enacted law and follows prescribed procedures. A substantive approach also asks whether the legal order protects basic rights and guards against profoundly arbitrary or oppressive exercises of power. Constitutional systems differ in how strongly they incorporate substantive review, so an answer should connect general theory with the specific constitutional text being discussed.

items.text: Constitutional law deals with the creation of state institutions, distribution of public power, limits on that power and protection of rights. It is therefore both structural and rights-oriented.

Constitutional conventions are recurring political practices that help institutions operate even when they are not enforced in the same way as ordinary legal rules. Their importance is practical and constitutional rather than merely social.
Rule of law requires public officials to act under law, through lawful authority and subject to legal accountability. It is the opposite of arbitrary rule based only on personal will.

Due process expresses the idea that state action affecting important interests must follow lawful and fair procedures. In constitutional analysis, explain notice, opportunity to be heard, impartial decision-making and lawful authority where relevant.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not treat rule of law as only “everyone is equal.” Equality is important, but rule of law also concerns legality, non-arbitrariness, accountability and fair legal process.

items.text: Prepare one precise definition for each concept.
Use short examples from parliamentary and judicial practice.
Explain both formal legality and substantive protection where relevant.

segments.text: Conventions may be politically binding even when not judicially enforceable.
Rule of law rejects arbitrary government.
Due process connects state action with lawful and fair procedure.
